text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Confusion arises over the missing persons shown in a picture on a private television station. Two people have identified themselves in the picture.
- Direct talks between the two sides on the Cyprus problem are expected to start at the end of May or at the beginning of June.
- Basketball players suspected of a vicious attack on a policeman are remanded for a further eight days.
- Talks are closer to starting, but mistrust between the two communities is a major problem, says Kester Heaslip, the E.U. Presidency representative on Cyprus.
- Spot foreign exchange transactions by local banks reached four million pounds in 1996.
- Two new floatations are expected on the Cyprus Stock Exchange in April and July.
- Different interpretations on the ownership of the Church-controlled Hellenic Mining Company is referred to the attorney-general.
- Direct talks will be held in Cyprus sooner or later, says the government spokesman.
- Cyprus's economy should be reunified, say Turkish and Greek Cypriot trade unions.
- Nicosia sees direct talks approaching. The government is no longer talking of "common ground" being a prerequisite for the resumption of talks.
- Eight thousand civil servants threaten to strike if a supplementary budget on the restructure of 12 government departments is not approved.
- Unnecessary confusion breaks out over the question of missing persons in a picture. Two people are claiming the identity of one man shown in the photo.
